A study by (Sanzana, et al., 2023), investigated the effectiveness of virtual labs 
in on student satisfaction. The study engaged 91 students from the University of 
Nottingham Malaysia, in either virtual or physical labs. The study found a 
significant positive affect with 31.43% of students showing an increased level of 
interest in the subject with virtual labs verses the 21.43% with the traditional 
labs. Students that used the virtual labs showed an enhanced level of comfort, 
and engagement. The paper did not conduct an exam to demonstrate increased 
knowledge or understanding. 
A paper by (Tamás & Miklós, 2018) investigates the potential advantages and 
disadvantages of virtual laboratories. Clear advantages of virtual laboratories are 
that they can be completed anywhere and are not confined to safety limits and 
regulations. However they limit a student’s exposure to real laboratory 
equipment, which may result worse real-world performance. 
Without a large-scale meta-analysis, the effectiveness of virtual laboratories is 
unknown. However, this does not rule out their need since students that may 
not have access to a laboratory or are unable to producing the 
experiment/scenario, may benefit from indirect experience over nothing. Virtual 
laboratories show an increased level of engagement, however, this maybe 
simply due to the new experience and after extended exposure the novelty may 
wear off.
